Hi Alex / Sarah —

Thanks for the clear asks. Quick answers + proposed technical plan below. Happy to walk through on the call.

1) Auth / SDK- OIDC: Redwood supports OIDC-based short-lived tokens via our private deployment and dedicated customers today. For hosted customers we can accept OIDC assertions through our token exchange endpoint + short-lived API tokens (standard pattern). We’ll document exact token exchange flow and sample code.

2) SDKs with native routing policy support- Python and Node SDKs both support client-side routing policies (v2 SDKs). Server-side (on our control plane) policy configs are authored as YAML and pushed to the runtime; SDKs can fetch and cache policy configs. We have example repos: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-examples (I’ll point to the routing-policy sample in the doc).

3) Model routing + fallback heuristics- Policy knobs we recommend:
  • latency_threshold_ms: e.g., 300 (P95) - if runtime observes > threshold, route to next model in chain.
  • cost_budget_per_1000: used for background reranking/batch jobs to pick quantized/cheaper variants.
  • region_pin: optional flag to force a customer’s requests to a region (eu-west-1) and set fallback variants within same region.
  • circuit_breaker: max_consecutive_errors before switching to a fallback.

Fallback chain example (from our routing-policy diagram):
  - primary: redwood-chat-4b-lowlat (regional)
  - secondary: redwood-chat-8b-cost (if latency spikes or malformed prompt)
  - tertiary: redwood-chat-20b-highqual (only for high-quality route or manual override)

Policy is evaluated at the routing proxy and supports per-customer overrides. The runtime emits tracing for each routing decision (model chosen, reason, latency, cost_estimate).

4) Structured output & tool-calling- We recommend enforced schema verification at the proxy layer (validate JSON schema returned from model). For tool-calling, Redwood provides a tool sandboxing layer: tools are registered in a manifest and model outputs are matched against tool invocation patterns. We can enable strict mode where only pre-approved tools are callable.

5) Embeddings & reranker flow- Best practice: run a small, cost-effective embedding model for initial vectorization (redwood-embed-2x) and use a learned reranker (lightweight cross-encoder) that runs only on the top-K retrieved candidates to save token cost. We can provide a sample pipeline (embedding -> FAISS -> rerank).

Proposed spike for your infra team:
- I’ll provide a sample policy YAML and a Docker-based policy-testing harness.
- We’ll set up a staging route: 90% traffic to primary, 10% to fallback chain for 48 hours; collect latency/cost metrics and adjust thresholds.

Scheduling: Thurs 11/3 10:00 PT works for me - Marissa / Marcus, can you confirm?

Thanks,
